The correct answer is A! Excessive vitamin E (found in nuts) inhibits the body's ability to absorb vitamin A. Symptoms of vitamin A deficiency include night blindness Therefore, this patient is suffering from  - a) Vitamin A deficiency caused by excessive vitamin E- in his diet.  Why is this important? Vitamin A is a water-soluble vitamin, which the body cannot effectively remove from it's system. In very high levels it can cause: Hypervitaminosis A - Liver damage - Skull and eye deformities in foetuses- Increased cancer sensitivity- Increased blood pressure Other symptoms of vitamin A deficiency include: - Pinpoint pupils (due to reduced rhodopsin production)- Increased intracranial pressure- Abnormal/sparse hair- impaired immunity- Increased amounts of mucus (leading to conjunctivitis and a runny nose)- Abnormal bone formation (leading to fractures from minor trauma)- Reduced cell growth and reproduction- Reduced total body heat production (leading to hypothermia)
